keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the cause (Gutenberg's press could print hundreds of identical pages quickly) and the conclusion (it changed how knowledge was created, shared, and controlled). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why did more ordinary people have reasons to learn to read?
qs.qko: 왜 더 많은 평범한 사람들이 글 읽기를 배울 이유가 생겼나요?
evs: As books became cheaper, more ordinary people had reasons to learn to read.
A single book could take months to produce, so only churches, universities, and wealthy people owned many of them.
Printing also helped standardize spelling and grammar in many languages.
New religious and political ideas also spread faster than authorities could control them.
why: 본문에 «As books became cheaper» 라고 나와요. 책값이 싸지자 평범한 사람들도 읽기를 배울 이유가 생겼어요.
The text says that as books became cheaper, more ordinary people had reasons to learn to read.

qs.q: In 'Printing also helped standardize spelling and grammar,' what does 'standardize' mean?
qs.qko: 'Printing also helped standardize spelling and grammar' 에서 'standardize' 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: make things follow the same rules everywhere
evs: Printing also helped standardize spelling and grammar in many languages.
Gutenberg's press made it possible to print hundreds of identical pages quickly.
Before then, most books in Europe were copied by hand, a slow and expensive process.
For example, Martin Luther's writings in the early 1500s reached a wide audience thanks to printed pamphlets.
why: 인쇄기는 «똑같은(identical)» 페이지를 수백 장 찍었어요. 같은 글이 널리 퍼지면서 철자와 문법도 어디서나 같아졌다는 뜻이에요.
The press printed hundreds of identical pages, so spelling and grammar became the same everywhere.

qs.q: How did the printing press help science move forward?
opts: Exact copies let scientists share findings, and others could check and build on them
Gutenberg himself made many new scientific discoveries
Only scientists were allowed to print books
evs: Gutenberg's press made it possible to print hundreds of identical pages quickly.
Scientists could share their findings accurately, and others could check and build on their work.
Around 1450, Johannes Gutenberg developed a printing press with movable metal type in Germany.
New religious and political ideas also spread faster than authorities could control them.
why: 인쇄기는 똑같은 페이지를 빠르게 찍었고, 그래서 과학자들은 연구 결과를 정확하게 나누고 다른 사람들은 그것을 확인하고 이어 연구할 수 있었어요. 두 단서를 합치면 답이 나와요.
The press printed identical pages, so scientists could share findings accurately and others could check and build on them.
